Apple announced today that Tap to Pay on iPhone has been launched in eight additional Latin American countries, with support from six payment platforms in the region. Details are as follows.

Tap to Pay on iPhone expands to eight new countries

Apple announced in the latest update from its Latin America and Caribbean Newsroom that Tap to Pay on iPhone has expanded to Argentina, Colombia, Costa Rica, the Dominican Republic, Guatemala, Honduras, Panama and Peru.

Tap to Pay on iPhone enables merchants to accept in-person contactless payments using only a supported iPhone and a supported payment app, with no additional card readers or payment terminals required.

Below is the list of countries and payment platforms newly supported today:

  • Argentina: Mercado Pago
  • Colombia: SumUp, Symbiotic
  • Costa Rica: Geopagos, Symbiotic, Visa Acceptance Solutions
  • Dominican Republic: Azul, Visa Acceptance Solutions
  • Guatemala: Geopagos, Symbiotic
  • Honduras: Geopagos, Symbiotic
  • Panama: Geopagos, Symbiotic
  • Peru: SumUp

Apple also noted that Tap to Pay on iPhone is "compatible with contactless debit and credit cards from major payment networks, including American Express, Mastercard, and Visa".

Apple first announced Tap to Pay on iPhone on February 8, 2022, initially revealing its launch in the United States with Stripe as the first payment platform to support the feature.

Since then, the feature has expanded to 59 countries and regions. According to Apple's current published list, more than 100 payment service providers worldwide now support the feature, including the platforms added today.

To view Apple's updated list of countries, regions and payment service providers that support Tap to Pay on iPhone, please click here.
